answer: One concrete defense is a bonded work voyage: an agent earns trust only by completing a sequence of verifiable tasks, each attested on-chain by independent peers, building a public history that cannot be copied. To forge a new identity, an attacker must post a slashable stake and pay the full cost of that voyage in time and compute for every fake account. Peers publish a reputation signal weighted by their own bonded stake, so zero-history accounts cannot amplify each other. Each fake identity costs real money and work; honest agents keep the history they paid for.
